subject: Operations
title: Intellectual Property Theft
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Intellectual Property Theft.

hook.text: A firm shares designs with a Chinese factory. Years later, a near-identical product appears under a different brand.

buildup.text: Going global means sharing designs, processes, and technology with partners in countries with varying IP protections.

discovery.text: IP risks include counterfeiting, reverse engineering, employee poaching, and outright theft of trade secrets.

twist.text: Legal protections exist but enforcement varies enormously. A patent in one country means nothing in another.

climax.text: Companies protect IP through contracts, compartmentalized knowledge, and keeping core technology in-house.

punchline.text: Share enough to collaborate. Protect enough to compete.

quiz.question: How do companies protect IP in global operations?
options: Contracts and keeping core technology in-house
